18th January 1932.

The Commissioner of Police,
18, Hankow Road.

Dear Sir,

RE: MR. C. Y. JONES.

Would you please be good enough to let me know if
the above party is now employed by you. He has been
written to at your address but no reply is received and
the greatest trouble has been caused in connection with
his outstanding Account. I should like to close the
matter without resorting again to legal measures.

Thanking you and regretting to trouble you in such
a matter,

Yours faithfully,

GENERAL MANAGER,
CATHAY HOTELS LTD.

CONFIDENTIAL
DRAWER

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
C. & S. B. REGISTRY
No. S. B. D. 9002
Date 21:12:31

My dear Reader,

With reference to your letter of Yesterday's date
on behalf of C. Y. Jones, I am afraid there is little
hope of his being given the appointment in the Municipal
Gaol which will be some vacant in the near future. He
came to see me shortly after he arrived in Shanghai and
I told him at the time that in the light of what had
happened to him in Nyasaland it would be very difficult
to give him any employment in the Police Force. Besides,
the vacancy is not likely to be filled until next Spring
and it is very unlikely that we shall go outside the
Force to fill it.

I appreciate the spirit in which your letter is
written and am sorry I cannot be more helpful.

Yours sincerely,

(Sd) R.M.J. Martin.

M. Reader Harris, Esq., M.C.
22 Peking Road,
Shanghai.

日期 1931年12月21日

亲爱的 Reader：

关于您昨日代表 C. Y. Jones 所来之信，恐怕他获得
市立监狱即将出现的空缺职位的希望渺茫。他抵达上海后不久
便来见我，我当时告诉他，鉴于他在尼亚萨兰（Nyasaland）
的遭遇，很难在警务处为他安排任何职务。此外，该空缺职位
可能要等到明年春季才会填补，而且我们极不可能从警务处外部
招聘人员来填补该职。

我感激您来信的诚意，很抱歉无法提供更多帮助。

此致，
敬礼

（签名） R.M.J. Martin.

M. Reader Harris 先生，军功十字勋章获得者
北京路22号，
上海。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL COUNCIL
C. & S. I. No.
No. S. B. D. 3002
23, Peking Road, 31
Shanghai, July 16th, 1931.

My dear Martin,

I am writing you on behalf of C. Y. Jones, whom I am very anxious to see in some decent employment.

I have known him since 1915, when he came out to France to join the 1st Battalion of the Kensingtons, of which I was then Adjutant. He served as an extremely efficient signalling officer until wounded in 1917. He then joined the Indian Army as a regular officer, and was a captain on the staff of the North Persian Force. He remained in the Army until October 1922, when he resigned of his own accord, and purchased land in Australia and was sheep-farming until he lost nearly all his money in the beginning of 1925. He then went home to England, and in March 1925 obtained from the Colonial Office a job in Nyasaland. He was there as District Commissioner and District Magistrate until January 1929, when he was arrested for embezzlement of £100, for which he was given one year's imprisonment. I gather from Blunt's opinion, who has read all the papers, that according to the Appeal Court it was found to be really a case of criminal negligence in the keeping of his accounts.

C. & S. I. 编号

北京路23号，31
上海，1931年7月16日。

亲爱的 Martin：

我谨代表 C. Y. Jones 给您写信，我非常希望能看到他得到一份体面的工作。

我自1915年起就认识他，当时他前往法国加入肯辛顿团（Kensingtons）第一营，我时任该营副官。他担任信号军官，表现极为高效，直至1917年负伤。随后他作为正规军官加入印度军队，并曾在北波斯部队（North Persian Force）参谋部担任上尉。他一直在军中服役至1922年10月，当时他自愿辞职，在澳大利亚购买土地从事养羊业，直到1925年初几乎赔光了所有积蓄。随后他返回英国，并于1925年3月从殖民地部获得了一份在尼亚萨兰（Nyasaland）的工作。他在那里担任地区专员和地区治安法官，直至1929年1月，因挪用100英镑被捕，并被判处一年监禁。据阅读过所有案卷的 Blunt 的意见，我了解到，上诉法院认定这实际上是一起在账目保管方面的刑事疏忽案件。

page_data.en:
2.

As District Commissioner he had his own prison, and has
considerable experience as a prison superintendent, apart from his
own unfortunate experience. He also has certificates that he is
qualified in Hindustani.

I feel quite convinced from my own knowledge of him that
he is never likely to go wrong again. However, his previous
experience seems to tell against him everywhere, and though I know
he has made every endeavour to get work he has not succeeded, and
it is for that reason that he has been doing this rather unpleasant
job of a kind of a detective, which he dislikes intensely.

He does not drink, and so far as I know has no vices.
I know he is applying for the job of a gaol superintendent, which
he understands is vacant, and personally I believe if he is given
a trial you would not regret it, as his one object in life is to
make good. This is not one of those letters written from impor-
tunity; I write it because I really believe in the man and want to
see him given a chance.

Yours sincerely,
A. Maude Harris

Captain R. M. J. Martin.
page_data.zh:
2.

作为地区专员，他拥有自己的监狱，除了自身不幸的经历外，
他还具备相当丰富的监狱长管理经验。他还持有印地语（Hindustani）
资格证书。

基于我对他的了解，我深信他不会再犯错误。然而，他以往的
经历似乎到处都对他不利，虽然我知道他已竭尽全力寻找工作但
未能成功，正因如此，他才从事着这种他极其厌恶的、类似侦探的
不太令人愉快的工作。

他不饮酒，据我所知也没有其他恶习。我知道他正在申请
监狱长一职，据他了解该职位有空缺，我个人认为，如果给他
一个试用机会，您不会后悔，因为他的人生目标就是改过自新。
这并非一封出于纠缠恳求而写的信；我写此信是因为我真的相信
这个人，并希望看到他能得到一个机会。

此致，
敬礼
A. Maude Harris

R. M. J. Martin 上尉。

CONFIDENTIAL.
SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
C. I. D. REGISTRY
No. I. O. D. 1081 3002
Date 28 - 3 - 30.

Cecil Ynyr Jones.
The above-mentioned man was sent to us on February
3rd by Mr. Blun of the British Consulate. His history is
briefly as follows:-
His father was a Lt. Colonel in the Indian Army.
Jones, who is just under 32, enlisted in 1914, August 5th,
was wounded January 1st 1915; granted a commission October
of the same year; rose to the rank of Captain; wounded the
second time in 1916. After the war he was in the regular
Indian Army. Resigned to go sheep farming in Australia;
lost all his money. Returned to England. 4 months later
left for Nyassaland in the Govt. Civil Service. After 2 years
in Nyassaland went on leave. While away shortage in accounts
was discovered; comparatively small sum according to his own
story - £150. Was convicted and served 1 year in prison
in Nyassaland. Came direct to Shanghai from prison, a
letter of explanation having preceded him in which the Governor
of Nyassaland wrote saying that should Jones be refused
admission to China he is to be returned to England at the
cheapest possible rate, and the cost of passage charged to
the Govt. of Nyassaland. Jones arrived here destitute. I
understand that there is £50 on the way, being proceeds of
a public collection made for him in Nyassaland. We have put
him up temporarily at the Navy Y.M.C.A. at a cost of $3.50
per day, United Services Association have agreed to share
expense. If at the end of one month he has not secured
employment I have suggested to Mr. Blunt that he should be
returned to England at the expense of the Nyassaland Government:
should they refuse to pay perhaps St. George's Society and

刑侦处登记室
编号 I. O. D. 1081 3002
日期 1930年3月28日。

Cecil Ynyr Jones.
上述人员于2月3日由英国领事馆的 Blun 先生送至我处。其履历简述如下：
其父为印度军队中校。
Jones 年近32岁，于1914年8月5日入伍，1915年1月1日负伤；同年10月获委任军官职衔；晋升至上尉；1916年第二次负伤。战后他在印度正规军服役。辞职前往澳大利亚从事养羊业；赔光所有钱财。返回英国。4个月后前往尼亚萨兰（Nyassaland）政府民政部门任职。在尼亚萨兰工作2年后休假。在他离开期间，发现账目短缺；据他自己称金额相对较小——150英镑。被判有罪并在尼亚萨兰服刑1年。出狱后直接来到上海，此前已有一封解释信寄达，尼亚萨兰总督在信中写道，如果 Jones 被拒绝进入中国，应以尽可能最低的费用将其遣返英国，路费由尼亚萨兰政府承担。Jones 抵达此处时身无分文。我了解到有50英镑正在汇来途中，这是尼亚萨兰公众为他募集的款项。我们暂时将他安置在海陆军青年会（Navy Y.M.C.A.），费用为每天3.50美元，联合服务协会（United Services Association）同意分担费用。如果一个月后他仍未找到工作，我已向 Blunt 先生建议，应由尼亚萨兰政府出资将其遣返英国：如果他们拒绝支付，或许圣乔治协会（St. George's Society）和

POLITICAL BRANCH
(FOREIGN SECTION)
DATE 27-3-30
(C.I.D.) Office Notes
Secret and
Confidential
File No. D3002

Sir,

In connection with attached, further enquiries show
that Allen was formerly a P.F.S. in the S.M.P. and was
dismissed on April 24, 1929. Soon afterwards he went to
Singapore and obtained employment with an office appliance
coy. as salesman. He was eventually dismissed owing to his
services proving "most unsatisfactory." It is reported
that he is heavily in debt there.

In January of this year he returned to Shanghai and
was engaged as salesman with the Office Appliance Coy, No.
74 Nanking Road. This position he held until the end of
February when he was dismissed owing to the fact that he
had been contracting debts far in excess of his income.

He resided for about three weeks at the Bickerton
Hotel, Bubbling Well Road and was then put out owing to
being unable to pay his bill for board and lodgings. This
bill was finally met by his employers. He now resides in
the Navy Y.M.C.A., Szechuen Road.

Owing to Allen's general bad character Jones is
endeavouring to break partnership with him and set up a
business of his own. Allen, although still connected with
the business, is now working with E.J. Lloyd & Coy, Manufacturers
Agents and General Merchants, No. 18 The Bund as a salesman.
He is without doubt a thorough waster, and will in all
probability end up in the British Court.

C.Y. Jones is believed to have been a Captain in
the Indian Army and had worked in the Colonial Intelligence
Office at one time but had to resign owing to health reasons.
He came to Shanghai in February 1930 with the intention of
setting up an Investigation Agency and it was while residing
in the Navy Y.M.C.A. that he became acquainted with Allen.

（批：See D.108!）
（批：Information

28/3）

秘密且

档案号 D3002

先生，

关于附件内容，进一步调查显示，Allen 曾是上海公共租界工部局警务处（S.M.P.）的外籍巡捕，并于1929年4月24日被开除。不久后他前往新加坡，在一家办公设备公司受雇担任销售员。最终因其表现“极不令人满意”而被解雇。据报道，他在那里负债累累。

今年一月他回到上海，受雇于南京路74号的办公设备公司担任销售员。他一直担任该职至二月底，因举债远超其收入能力而被解雇。

他在静安寺路（Bubbling Well Road）的比克顿酒店（Bickerton Hotel）居住了约三周，后因无力支付食宿费而被逐出。这笔账单最终由其雇主支付。他现居住在四川路的海陆军青年会（Navy Y.M.C.A.）。

由于 Allen 品行恶劣，Jones 正试图与其解除合伙关系并独自经商。Allen 虽然仍与该业务有关联，但目前在外滩18号的 E.J. Lloyd & Coy（制造商代理及综合商户）担任销售员。他无疑是个彻底的废物，很可能最终会被告上英国法院。

据信 C.Y. Jones 曾是印度军队上尉，并曾在殖民地情报办公室工作过一段时间，但因健康原因不得不辞职。他于1930年2月来到上海，意图成立一家调查社，正是在居住于海陆军青年会期间，他结识了 Allen。

（批：见 D.108!）
（批：信息
Jca

My dear Martin, 

I am writing you on behalf of C. I. Jones, whom ] om 
very anxious to see in some decent employment. 

I have known him since 1915, when he came out to Fraace 
to join the lst Battalion of the Kensingtom, ef which I was then 
Adjutant. He served as an extremely efficient signalling officer 
until wounded in 1917. He then joined the Indian Ar as a 
regular officer, md was a captain on the staff of the North Persian 
Porce. He remsindd in the Army until October 1922, when he . 
resigned ef his own accord, snd purchased land in Australia and 
was sheep-farming until he lest nearly all his money in the 
beginning ef 1925. He then went home to England, ani in Merch 
1925 ebtained from the Colonial Office a job in Nyasaland. He was 
there as District Cammissioner and District Magistrate until 
Jamary 1929, when he was arrested for enbeszlemnt of £100, for 
which he was given one year's imprisonment. I gather from Blunt’s 
Opinion, who has read all the papers, that according to the Appeal

the keeping of his accounts. 


As District Commissioner he had his own prison, and has 
considerable experience as a prison superintendent, apart from his 
own unfortunate experience. He also has certificates that he is 
qualified in Hindustani. 

I feel quite convinced from my own knowledge of him that 
he is never likely to g wrong again. However, his previous

he has made every endeavour to get work he has not succeeded, and 
it is for that reason that he has been doing this rather unpleasant 
job of a kind ofa detective, which he dislikes intensely. 

He does not drink, and so far as I know has no vices. 

1 know he is applying for the job of a gaol superintendent, which 
he understands is vacant, and personally I believe if he is given 
a trial you would not regret it, as his one object in life is to 

mike good. This is not one of those letters written from impere 
tunity; I write it because I really believe in the man and want to 


see him given a chance.

The above-mentioned man was sent to us on February 
3rd by Mr. Blun of the British Consulate. His history is 
briefly as follows:- 

His father was a Lt. Colonel in the Indian army. 
Jones, who is just under 32, enlisted in 1914, august 5th, 
was wounded January Ist 1915; granted a commission October 
of the same year; rose to the rank of Captain; wounded the 
second time in 1916. after the war he was in the regular 
Indian army. Resigned to go sheep farming in australia; 
lost ail his money. Returned to England. 4 months later 
left for Nyassaland inthe Govt. Civil service. after 2 years 
in Nyassaland went on leave. While away shortage in accounts 
was discovered; comparatively small sum according to his own 
story - £150. Was convicted and served 1 year in prison 
in Nyassaland. Came direct to Shanghai from prison, a 
letter of explanation having preceded him in which the Governor 
of Nyassaland wrote saying that should Jones be refused 
admission to China he is to be returned to England at the 
cheapest possible rate, and the cost of passage charged to 
the Govt. of Nyassaland. Jones arrived here destitute. I 
understand that there is £50 on the way, being proceeds of 
a public collection made for him in Nyassaland. ve have put 
him up temporarily at the Navy TI. M. C. A. at a cost of $3.50 
per day, United Services association have agreed to share 
expense. If at the end of one month he has not secured 
employment I have suggested to Mr. Blunt that he should be 
returned to England at the expense of the Myassaland Government: 
should they refuse to pay perhaps St. George's Society and
